content.title: About
content.content: Pomelo (Citrus maxima) is the largest citrus fruit, native to Southeast Asia. It has a very thick yellow-green rind, firm segments covered in a bitter membrane, and juicy flesh from pale yellow to pink. The flavor is sweet with a light tartness, milder than grapefruit. Pomelo is eaten fresh and added to salads and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pomelo is the largest of the citrus fruits: a fruit can weigh more than a kilogram.
Grapefruit is a hybrid of pomelo and orange.
Before eating, the thick rind and the bitter membrane on the segments must be removed.
In China and other Asian countries, pomelos are given at Lunar New Year and the Mid-Autumn Festival as a symbol of prosperity.
The rind of pomelo is made into candied peel and added to tea.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and skin.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and helps you feel full.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Pomelo is low in calories and high in water.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Pomelo, like grapefruit, can affect how some medications work, such as statins and blood pressure drugs; if you take medications, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Pomelo is acidic and may cause heartburn or irritate tooth enamel.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: People with kidney disease who need to limit potassium should consult a doctor.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Citrus fruits can cause allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut off the top, score the thick rind on the sides and peel it, separate the fruit into segments, and remove the bitter membrane, leaving only the flesh. Eat the flesh fresh, or add it to salads, yogurt, desserts, and juices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: A whole pomelo can be stored at room temperature for one to two weeks or longer in the refrigerator. Keep peeled segments in the refrigerator in a covered container for three to four days.
